messages:
Mia: Quick question — compliance emailed asking us to remove recent ephemeral request logs for customer ACME from local request-cache + memcached. What's the approved path for a one-off sweep? Do we need sec sign-off or can ops run a targeted flush?

Sam: Short answer: ops can flush caches, but anything that touches traces or S3 needs sec/legal. For memcached/local cache: we do a targeted sweep and record an audit entry. See policy: https://redwood.internal/security/data-retention#cache-sweeps

Jordan: Who signs off for the audit? Also what's the exact command so ops doesn't do a blanket flush by mistake.

Sam: Approvals: Data Access Group (Ana) or on-call security. Command we usually use (ops only):

```
rb-logctl sweep \  
  --customer-id=ACME \  
  --scope=request-cache,memcached \  
  --filter="request_id:12345 OR since:2026-03-01" \  
  --record-audit=true
```

Sam: That will only touch cache keys matched by filter. Do NOT run `rb-cache flush-all` — that takes down prod caches.

security_bot: NOTE: If traces or archived request blobs in S3 are implicated, escalate with a DSR ticket and sec/legal approval required. Ticket template: https://redwood.internal/sec/dsr-template

Mia: @Ana can you approve a cache-only sweep for ACME? We'll attach the audit entry and results.

Ana: OK — I approve cache-only sweep for ACME. Conditions: 1) No trace IDs in the sweep filter, 2) Attach audit record and S3 scan result showing no archived blobs. If you find traces, stop and escalate. :white_check_mark: 

Jordan: Got it. We'll run the rb-logctl sweep with the filter and post audit output here. Will ping if traces show up.

Sam: Small note — memcached TTL is 48h by default for request-cache, so if it's in that window we can just document and let it expire, but for compliance requests we still perform sweep to be safe.

Mia: Thanks. Scheduling ops run for 22:30 UTC and will paste the audit log after.

ops-bot: job/17433 scheduled by Jordan — rb-logctl sweep --customer-id=ACME --scope=request-cache,memcached --filter='since:2026-03-01' — ETA 2026-03-17T22:30:00Z

Mia: Closing loop after audit. Appreciate the quick thumbs up everyone. :thumbsup:
